```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("GarrazaObaldia_2024_propofol_remifentanil"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("GarrazaObaldia_2024_propofol_remifentanil"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics16121615> (open access)
* Supplement: <https://www.mdpi.com/article/10.3390/pharmaceutics16121615/s1>

Garraza-Obaldia et al. modelled mean arterial pressure (MAP) and heart rate
(HR) in women anaesthetised with target-controlled infusions (TCI) of propofol
and remifentanil. Both responses are turnover (indirect-response) states:

* propofol inhibits MAP production with an Emax function of its predicted
  plasma concentration (the Hill coefficient was not different from 1 and was
  removed);
* remifentanil inhibits HR production with a sigmoid Emax function of its
  predicted plasma concentration and has no direct effect on MAP;
* HR relative to its baseline feeds back on MAP production as
  `(HR / HR0)^FBHR`; the reverse feedback (MAP on HR) was not supported;
* the surgical stimulus (hysteroscopy) multiplies MAP production by
  `1 + thetaStim * exp(-kStim * (t - tStim))` from the start of surgery.

The drug exposures are the plasma concentrations that the TCI pumps predicted
from the Schnider (propofol) and Minto (remifentanil) PK models; nothing was
assayed. The packaged model therefore has no PK states. The concentrations
enter as the time-varying covariates `CP_PROPOFOL_UGML` (ug/mL) and
`CP_REMIFENTANIL_NGML` (ng/mL), and the start of surgery as the time-fixed
covariate `T_SURG_START` (min). Time is in minutes.

# Population

The analysis used 77 ASA I-II women having outpatient gynaecological surgery
at Hospital Clinic de Barcelona; three patients with chronic hypertension were
excluded from the 80 enrolled (Results; Table 1). The model was fitted to the
56-patient training group, all of whom had hysteroscopy (mean age 42 years,
SD 11; mean weight 62 kg, SD 9; mean BMI 24 kg/m^2, SD 4). The 21-patient test
group (other procedures) was used for external validation. Patients were
assigned to four step-up / step-down TCI schemes: propofol alone, remifentanil
alone, steady propofol with varying remifentanil, and steady remifentanil with
varying propofol (Section 2.1; Table S1). MAP was measured non-invasively every
minute and HR by continuous ECG. Age, weight, BMI, surgery duration, patient
position and stimulus type were screened as covariates and none was retained.

# Source trace

| Element | Value in model | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| MAP turnover ODE | `d/dt(map) = kin_map (1 - f) (hr/rbase_hr)^fb_hr h_stim - kout_map map` | Equation (1); Figure 2B |
| HR turnover ODE | `d/dt(hr) = kin_hr (1 - g) - kout_hr hr` | Equation (2); Figure 2B (MAP feedback on HR dropped, Section 3.1) |
| Production rates | `kin = kout * baseline` | Section 2.4 (steady state); derived 10.8 mmHg/min and 8.7 bpm/min in Section 3.1 |
| Propofol effect `f` | Emax, no Hill exponent | Equation (3); gamma removed (Section 3.1); Figure 2B |
| Remifentanil effect `g` | sigmoid Emax | Equation (4); Figure 2B |
| HR feedback `p` | `(hr/rbase_hr)^fb_hr` | Equation (5) |
| Stimulus `h` | `1 + emax_stim exp(-kstim (t - T_SURG_START))`, 1 before | Equation (7); Figure 2B |
| `lec50_propofol` | log(8.79) ug/mL | Table 2, C50Propo |
| `logitemax_propofol` | logit(0.88) | Table 2, EmaxPropo; logistic constraint (Section 2.4) |
| `lec50_remifentanil` | log(4.57) ng/mL | Table 2, C50Remi |
| `logitemax_remifentanil` | logit(0.69) | Table 2, EmaxRemi,HR |
| `lhill_remifentanil` | log(1.20) | Table 2, gammaRemi |
| `lrbase_map` | log(88.2) mmHg | Table 2, MAP0 |
| `lrbase_hr` | log(70.8) bpm | Table 2, HR0 |
| `lkout` | log(0.123) 1/min | Table 2, kout (one typical value for MAP and HR, Section 3.1) |
| `lfb_hr` | log(0.806) | Table 2, FBHR |
| `lkstim` | log(0.021) 1/min | Table 2, kStim |
| `lemax_stim` | log(0.284) | Table 2, thetaStim |
| `etalec50_propofol`, `etalkout_map` block | 0.733137, 0.76, 1.109710 | Table 2: IIV 104.0% and 142.6% CV; covariance 0.76 |
| `etalec50_remifentanil` | 0.730139 | Table 2, IIV C50Remi 103.7% CV |
| `etalrbase_map` | 0.00742009 | Table 2, IIV MAP0 8.63% CV |
| `etalrbase_hr` | 0.0205239 | Table 2, IIV HR0 14.4% CV |
| `etalkout_hr` | 0.991474 | Table 2, IIV kout,HR 130.2% CV |
| `etalkstim` | fixed(0.693147) | Section 3.1: variance held at the equivalent of a 100% CV |
| `addSd_map` | 5.53 mmHg | Table 2, residual error in MAP |
| `addSd_hr` | 4.30 bpm | Table 2, residual error in HR |

The IIV variances use `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`, the inverse of the CV
definition in the footnote of Table 2 (`CV = sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)`).

# Deterministic checks

```{r load-model}
mod <- readModelDb("GarrazaObaldia_2024_propofol_remifentanil")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
th <- ui$theta
```

## Derived production rates and stimulus half-life

The paper reports the derived production rates and the half-life of the
stimulus effect.

```{r derived}
derived <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c("kin,MAP (mmHg/min)", "kin,HR (bpm/min)", "Stimulus half-life (min)"),
  Model = c(
    exp(th[["lkout"]]) * exp(th[["lrbase_map"]]),
    exp(th[["lkout"]]) * exp(th[["lrbase_hr"]]),
    log(2) / exp(th[["lkstim"]])
  ),
  Paper = c(10.8, 8.7, 33)
)
knitr::kable(derived, digits = 2, caption = "Derived quantities quoted in Results Sections 3.1 and 3.4 and the Discussion.")
stopifnot(all(abs(derived$Model / derived$Paper - 1) < 0.01))
```

## Steady state under constant concentrations

With constant drug concentrations and no stimulus, both ODEs settle at

* `HR_ss = HR0 * (1 - g(CRemi))`
* `MAP_ss = MAP0 * (1 - f(CPropo)) * (1 - g(CRemi))^FBHR`

The typical-value model is solved to 600 min (about 100 half-lives of `kout`)
over a grid of concentrations and compared with this closed form.

```{r steady-state}
ss_grid <- tidyr::expand_grid(cp = c(0, 2, 4, 8), cr = c(0, 1, 2, 4)) |>
  mutate(id = row_number())
ss_events <- ss_grid |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = c(0, 600)) |>
  transmute(
    id, time,
    evid = 0, amt = 0,
    CP_PROPOFOL_UGML = cp,
    CP_REMIFENTANIL_NGML = cr,
    T_SURG_START = 1e6
  ) |>
  arrange(id, time)

ss_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(ui), ss_events,
  rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12, returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  filter(time == 600)

emax_p <- plogis(th[["logitemax_propofol"]])
ec50_p <- exp(th[["lec50_propofol"]])
emax_r <- plogis(th[["logitemax_remifentanil"]])
ec50_r <- exp(th[["lec50_remifentanil"]])
hill_r <- exp(th[["lhill_remifentanil"]])
fb <- exp(th[["lfb_hr"]])

ss_check <- ss_grid |>
  mutate(
    f = emax_p * cp / (cp + ec50_p),
    g = emax_r * cr^hill_r / (cr^hill_r + ec50_r^hill_r),
    hr_closed = exp(th[["lrbase_hr"]]) * (1 - g),
    map_closed = exp(th[["lrbase_map"]]) * (1 - f) * (1 - g)^fb
  ) |>
  left_join(select(ss_sim, id, map, hr), by = "id")

ss_check |>
  select(cp, cr, map, map_closed, hr, hr_closed) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Propofol (ug/mL)" = cp,
    "Remifentanil (ng/mL)" = cr,
    "MAP solved (mmHg)" = map,
    "MAP closed form (mmHg)" = map_closed,
    "HR solved (bpm)" = hr,
    "HR closed form (bpm)" = hr_closed
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical-value steady state against the closed form.")

# Same parameters on both sides, so only integration error separates them.
stopifnot(
  nrow(ss_check) == 16,
  max(abs(ss_check$map / ss_check$map_closed - 1)) < 1e-5,
  max(abs(ss_check$hr / ss_check$hr_closed - 1)) < 1e-5
)
```

Propofol at 4 ug/mL alone lowers the typical MAP by about 28%. Remifentanil
lowers MAP only through HR, and the HR feedback exponent below 1 damps that
effect.

# Replicating Figure 4: risk of hypotension

The paper simulated a 90-min procedure (Figure 1): induction targets until
10 min, maintenance targets until 80 min, then both targets set to zero, with
hysteroscopy starting at 20 min. Three schemes paired the two drugs at
different effect-site targets:

```{r schemes}
schemes <- tibble::tibble(
  scheme = 1:3,
  propofol_induction = c(4.0, 4.5, 5.0),
  remifentanil_induction = c(3.0, 2.5, 2.0),
  propofol_maintenance = c(2.5, 3.0, 3.5),
  remifentanil_maintenance = c(2.0, 1.5, 1.0)
)
schemes |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Scheme" = scheme,
    "Propofol induction (ug/mL)" = propofol_induction,
    "Remifentanil induction (ng/mL)" = remifentanil_induction,
    "Propofol maintenance (ug/mL)" = propofol_maintenance,
    "Remifentanil maintenance (ng/mL)" = remifentanil_maintenance
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Effect-site targets of the three schemes (Figure 1B).")
```

The model is driven by *plasma* concentrations, which the paper obtained by
running the Schnider and Minto TCI algorithms. Neither PK model is in this
package, so here the plasma concentration is set equal to the effect-site
target (a step function). At a constant target, a TCI pump holds plasma and
effect site at the same concentration. The approximation therefore differs
from the paper only during the few minutes after each target change. In those
minutes a real pump overshoots the plasma concentration on the way up and
stops infusing on the way down.

For each scheme 200 virtual patients are simulated (the paper used 1000).
Hypotension is defined as in the paper: MAP below 60 mmHg, or a fall of at
least 20% from the individual baseline `MAP0`. The probabilities use the
individual predicted MAP, without residual error.

```{r fig4-sim}
n_per_scheme <- 200
times <- 0:90

fig4_events <- schemes |>
  tidyr::crossing(subject = seq_len(n_per_scheme), time = times) |>
  mutate(
    id = (scheme - 1) * n_per_scheme + subject,
    evid = 0, amt = 0,
    CP_PROPOFOL_UGML = case_when(
      time < 10 ~ propofol_induction,
      time < 80 ~ propofol_maintenance,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    CP_REMIFENTANIL_NGML = case_when(
      time < 10 ~ remifentanil_induction,
      time < 80 ~ remifentanil_maintenance,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    T_SURG_START = 20
  ) |>
  select(id, time, evid, amt, CP_PROPOFOL_UGML, CP_REMIFENTANIL_NGML, T_SURG_START, scheme) |>
  arrange(id, time)

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20241215)
fig4_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  ui, fig4_events,
  covsInterpolation = "locf", keep = "scheme", returnType = "data.frame"
)

risk <- fig4_sim |>
  group_by(scheme, time) |>
  summarise(
    p_below60 = mean(map < 60),
    p_drop20 = mean(map <= 0.8 * rbase_map),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

```{r fig4-plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3.5}
risk |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(p_below60, p_drop20), names_to = "criterion", values_to = "probability") |>
  mutate(criterion = factor(
    criterion,
    levels = c("p_below60", "p_drop20"),
    labels = c("MAP < 60 mmHg", "20% decrease of MAP from baseline")
  )) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, probability, colour = factor(scheme))) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 20, xmax = 70, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~criterion, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Probability", colour = "Scheme") +
  theme_bw()
```

*Replicates Figure 4 of Garraza-Obaldia 2024. The grey band is the period of
surgery (20-70 min).*

The paper reports a maximum probability before surgery of 0.35 (MAP < 60 mmHg)
and 0.70 (20% decrease), just before surgery starts, and a maximum during and
after surgery of 0.38 and 0.65, at the end of surgery (Results Section 3.4).

```{r fig4-compare}
pool <- risk |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(p_below60 = mean(p_below60), p_drop20 = mean(p_drop20), .groups = "drop")
at <- function(tm, col) {
  v <- pool[[col]][pool$time == tm]
  if (length(v) != 1L) stop("no unique row at time ", tm)
  v
}
fig4_cmp <- tibble::tibble(
  Quantity = c(
    "P(MAP < 60), 20 min (start of surgery)",
    "P(20% decrease), 20 min (start of surgery)",
    "P(MAP < 60), 80 min (end of infusion)",
    "P(20% decrease), 80 min (end of infusion)"
  ),
  Simulated = c(at(20, "p_below60"), at(20, "p_drop20"), at(80, "p_below60"), at(80, "p_drop20")),
  Paper = c(0.35, 0.70, 0.38, 0.65)
)
knitr::kable(fig4_cmp, digits = 2, caption = "Peak hypotension risk, pooled over the three schemes (600 virtual patients), against Results Section 3.4.")

# Cohort proportions (600 patients pooled, binomial SE <= 0.02): a 0.15
# envelope admits sampling noise and the plasma = target approximation.
# A mis-transcribed C50, Emax or baseline would move them by more.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(fig4_cmp$Simulated - fig4_cmp$Paper) < 0.15),
  # The stimulus at 20 min cuts the risk sharply (Figure 4: about 0.70 -> 0.48).
  at(25, "p_drop20") < at(20, "p_drop20") - 0.1,
  # Risk recovers after the targets go to zero at 80 min.
  at(90, "p_drop20") < at(80, "p_drop20") - 0.2
)
```

As in the paper, the three schemes give nearly the same risk profile, and the
risk climbs during surgery as the stimulus effect wears off.

# Size of the surgical stimulus

The paper's abstract and Discussion describe the surgical stimulus as a
"predicted typical increase of 28 mmHg". In the model, `thetaStim` = 0.284 is
the fractional increase in MAP *production* at the start of surgery. The
typical-value MAP increase this produces is computed below, both without drugs
and under maintenance scheme 1, against the same subject without surgery.

```{r stimulus-size}
stim_events <- bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(id = 1, time = 0:180, CP_PROPOFOL_UGML = 0, CP_REMIFENTANIL_NGML = 0, T_SURG_START = 20),
  tibble::tibble(id = 2, time = 0:180, CP_PROPOFOL_UGML = 0, CP_REMIFENTANIL_NGML = 0, T_SURG_START = 1e6),
  tibble::tibble(id = 3, time = 0:180, CP_PROPOFOL_UGML = 2.5, CP_REMIFENTANIL_NGML = 2.0, T_SURG_START = 20),
  tibble::tibble(id = 4, time = 0:180, CP_PROPOFOL_UGML = 2.5, CP_REMIFENTANIL_NGML = 2.0, T_SURG_START = 1e6)
) |>
  mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0)

stim_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  rxode2::zeroRe(ui), stim_events,
  covsInterpolation = "locf", returnType = "data.frame"
)
stim_size <- stim_sim |>
  mutate(
    condition = ifelse(id <= 2, "No drugs", "Scheme 1 maintenance"),
    arm = ifelse(id %% 2 == 1, "surgery", "none")
  ) |>
  select(condition, arm, time, map) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = map) |>
  mutate(increase = surgery - none) |>
  group_by(condition) |>
  summarise(peak_increase = max(increase), time_of_peak = time[which.max(increase)], .groups = "drop")

stim_size |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Condition" = condition,
    "Peak MAP increase (mmHg)" = peak_increase,
    "Time of peak (min)" = time_of_peak
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Typical-value MAP increase caused by the surgical stimulus starting at 20 min.")
```

The typical individual's peak increase is well below 28 mmHg. The figure of 28
matches `thetaStim` = 0.284, a 28% increase in MAP production at the start of
surgery, so the paper's "28 mmHg" looks like that fraction quoted with the
wrong unit. The model uses the Table 2 estimate and is not adjusted.

# PKNCA

There is no NCA in this vignette. The model has no PK states: drug exposure is
an input covariate, and the outputs are haemodynamic responses. The checks
above (closed-form steady state, derived constants, and the Figure 4
replication) take its place.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Plasma concentrations in the simulations.** The paper drove the model with
  plasma concentrations predicted by the Schnider and Minto TCI algorithms.
  Those PK models are not in nlmixr2lib, so the Figure 4 replication sets
  plasma concentration equal to the effect-site target. This is exact at
  constant targets and approximate for a few minutes after each target change.
  Users with a TCI simulator should supply its predicted plasma concentrations
  in `CP_PROPOFOL_UGML` and `CP_REMIFENTANIL_NGML`.
* **Residual error in the hypotension probabilities.** The paper does not say
  whether its 1000 simulated MAP profiles included residual error. The
  probabilities here use individual predictions without it.
* **IIV on kStim.** Table 2 does not list it. Section 3.1 states that the
  variance was fixed to the equivalent of a 100% CV, which on the CV scale of
  the Table 2 footnote is `log(1 + 1^2) = log(2)`.
* **No IIV on Emax.** The Methods state that logistic models were used for IIV
  on the Emax parameters, but Table 2 reports no Emax variance, so the final
  model carries none. The Emax values are kept on the logit scale.
* **Covariance, not correlation.** Table 2 labels the C50Propo / kout,MAP
  entry (0.76) a covariance, and its bootstrap interval reaches 1.43, which a
  correlation cannot. It is encoded as a covariance (implied correlation
  0.84).
* **No end-of-surgery term.** Equation (7) has no offset at the end of surgery;
  the stimulus effect simply decays from its onset, as in the paper's
  simulations.
* **Other noxious stimuli.** Laryngeal-mask insertion, oesophageal
  instrumentation and tetanic stimulation had no identifiable effect and are
  not in the model, so the laryngeal-mask insertion at 5 min in Figure 1 needs
  no input.
* **Surgical-stimulus magnitude.** The "typical increase of 28 mmHg" in the
  abstract and Discussion is not reproduced (see above); the Table 2 estimate
  of `thetaStim` is used as published.
